mappings.notes: CONSUMER SET, re-derived at base_revision rather than taken from the map, whose Q3 enumeration was cut at an older revision and is INCOMPLETE. (i) The two importers Q3 names: results/io.py:16,380 (applied on every HDF5 read) and solver.py:205,10153 (applied on every run's get_results), both of which now return the namespace unwrapped. (ii) scripts/smoke_sim1d.py -- NOT the '4 smoke assertions' Q3 names, but five blocks across three cases (no-source-run-and-results, cathode-power-balance-warming, breakdown-retry-near-vacuum): a 20-name hasattr loop, roughly twenty alias-vs-source equalities, the HDF5 round-trip pairs, and the breakdown-time aliases. (iii) scripts/sweep_sim1d_stability.py:163,166 -- `result.cathode.I_tot` and `result.cathode_twin.I_tot`, a live executable consumer OUTSIDE the smoke that Q3 lists nowhere; migrated in this commit to cathode_diagnostics['source_I_tot'] / ['end_I_tot'], the rows those namespaces were built from, which are seeded NaN per end unconditionally so nanmax reads the same numbers. NO LOUD-ERROR SELECTOR IS OWED and the reason is structural: compat.py had no config key and no selector, it ran on every result, so no template key becomes meaningless and there is no route to refuse. The removal is loud regardless -- a result is a plain SimpleNamespace and each retired alias is an AttributeError at first read, never a silently wrong value. The retired surface, in full, is the 27 names in scripts/smoke_sim1d.py's _RETIRED_SIM3_COMPAT_ALIASES: ne, v_plasma, n_beam, cathode, cathode_twin, t_breakdown, t_breakdown_ms, time_since_breakdown, time_ms_since_breakdown, Ne_flux, Nn_flux, S_ion_bulk, S_ion_beam, S_rec_rad, S_rec_3b, Qie, Qei, Qen, Qcx, Qeb, Qib, e_par_flux, i_par_flux, e_perp_hl, i_perp_hl, sim3_compat_units, sim3_compat_notes. The smoke asserts every one of them ABSENT, on the run path and on the load path separately, so a re-added shim fails the gate.

Under the established 'manifest names its parent' pattern the carve's manifest-finalization commit (0d10eec, which created this file) and its staging merge (f353564) fall OUTSIDE the range the predecessor declares, so they land inside this delta's range instead. `git diff --name-status --no-renames 364b26d f353564` is exactly this one added path and nothing else -- a narrower bridge than the carve's, which had a delete/add pair. Without this row check (4) COVERAGE would fail on an add this commit did not make. Same open question the carve raised and the reviewer has not yet ruled: whether the pattern wants the bridging row, or wants the validator to tolerate a bookkeeping gap between a delta's declared new_revision and its successor's base.
